subject: Regional circuit cutover analysis and residency gating for EU/APAC private deploy

Subject: Multi-site residency gating + circuit-cutover scenarios (AstraHealth private deploy)

Sergio —

Thanks again for the architecture walkthrough last week. Our infra team consolidated a list of residency and failover questions that need to be signed off before we proceed with the private VPC deployment across EU and APAC. Attached is a short spreadsheet with our acceptance criteria and three cutover scenarios we want validated. High-level asks:

- Confirm explicit egress paths and control-plane call routing during an EU->APAC warm-standby failover.
- Define what constitutes a jurisdictional "circuit cut" (e.g., whole-region peering loss vs. partial SNAT failure) and Redwood's automated response for each.
- We need evidence artifacts for legal: TTLs for audit logs, KMS key residency, and proof of no cross-border logs during steady-state.

Can you route to the right folks and propose a short runbook we can review? We prefer a one-hour review session with network diagrams + a sanity test plan.

Attachments: astra_requirements_20270901.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — Marta

> Thanks again for the architecture walkthrough last week. Our infra team consolidated a list of residency and failover questions ...

Hi Marta — thanks for the detailed list. Looping in Hannah (residency controls lead), Jonas (networking/routing), and Vivek (private deploy ops) to scope answers and produce the runbook. Quick answers up-front while we pull artifacts:

1) Egress & control-plane routing during a warm standby: by default we route control-plane traffic to the control plane in the EU region when the customer's control-plane is provisioned in EU. For warm-standby, data-plane failover uses route policy RP-geo-pref (priority: eu-primary, apac-standby). If EU peering is lost entirely we fall back to apac-standby only when the health-check matrix marks eu-data-plane as degraded for 3 consecutive intervals (configurable). We will include a sequence diagram in the runbook.

2) Circuit definitions & automated responses: we've defined three fault classes in our internal runbooks — (A) full-region peering loss, (B) asymmetric reachability (partial SNAT/NAT gateway issues), (C) service-level packet loss above 7%. For A we trigger cross-region model handoff + alerting + read-only mode for control-plane actions. For B we attempt transient reroutes and prefix-level blackholing; for C we lower batching windows and enable locality fallback. We'll document exact probes and thresholds.

3) Evidence artifacts: Hannah will attach audit-log retention entries, KMS key residency attestations, and the filtered-sample log proving no cross-border log transfer in steady-state.

Proposed next steps:
- Hannah/Jonas/Vivek to produce a one-page runbook + sequence diagrams.
- 1-hour review session: Fri 2027-09-03 15:00 UTC (suggested), remote call + shared diagram.
- Deliverables before call: cutover-sequence-proposal.pdf, rdw-topology-diff.png, audit sample artifacts.

I'll follow up with the runbook draft by EOD Thu.

— Sergio
Sergio Álvarez

Sergio / Marta —

Quick thread with the runbook draft attached. Key points and clarifications:

- Cutover sequencing: we recommend staged cutover (0: control-plane failover validation in staging; 1: BGP prep and peering drain; 2: dataset-locality verification; 3: traffic switch; 4: post-cutover retention audit). The PDF has timestamps and explicit test queries.
- Circuit classification: we've formalized the definitions and included probe commands and expected outcomes (tcpdump snippets, curl health-check examples).
- Audit artifacts: sample retention logs are time-windowed and hashed; the KMS attestation lists key aliases and region tags. Note: the attestation is HSM-backed; legal requested a signed letter — we will produce that after the review call.

Attachments: cutover-sequence-proposal.pdf, rdw-topology-diff.png

Action items before our call on Fri:
- Jonas: finalize BGP prep checklist and SRE rollback commands.
- Vivek: prepare a small synthetic test we can run during the call to simulate partial SNAT failure (class B).
- Marta / Astra: confirm whether legal needs the signed attestation ahead of the test or it can be provided after a successful dry-run.

If the timeline looks tight we can move the call to Fri 16:00 UTC.

Thanks — Hannah
